assessment: A cover that seats correctly despite corner-shape differences and washing would be useful, but the observations do not establish how to achieve it. Rounded-corner installation failures support investigating corner accommodation; they do not explain the separate concentration of seam rework among larger covers.

openings.claim: Hypothesis: a concealed pleated corner pocket, closed with a washable cloth tie preset by the cooperative, could accommodate a measured rounded corner while preserving the ordered visible panel and allowing tool-free removal. The speculative capability is geometry-specific seating without exhibitor readjustment.
openings.delta: Replace fixed corner-pocket geometry with a small preset adjustment reserve. Dependencies are actual corner measurements, sufficient pocket travel after washing, stable tie settings, and a cutting layout that supplies the extra cloth. The presently testable partial capability is repeatable seating of one preset corner pocket.
openings.prediction: Compared with the current pocket, the preset pleated version will seat on a measured rounded corner without resetting its tie, both initially and after the stipulated five-cycle wash test. Failure to improve seating, or tie-setting drift, would count against the mechanism.
openings.probe: Obtain actual dimensions and corner measurements from willing customers, prioritizing nominal-only orders. Use retained offcuts to sew matched current and pleated corner samples. Compare repeated blind placements on the same measured customer corner if access is available; check tie movement, removal, and visible print disturbance before and after washing. Before batch adoption, time a complete pilot and measure the proposed layout waste by area. Proceed only within 350 units, two machines, three weeks, and 8% cutting waste; assess the final 40 against at least 38 first-placement fits, all ordered designs, and median working time at most 32 minutes.
assumptions: A customer can provide corner-test access beyond the offered measurements.
The purchased cloth can form durable, concealed pleats and ties.
Pilot material, preparation, and added sewing fit the resource and delivery limits.
